newsitem.title: QATAR: TENNIS-COURIER KNOCKS OUT MUSTER IN QATAR OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COURIER KNOCKS OUT MUSTER IN QATAR OPEN.

text.p: Jim Courier extended his stranglehold over Thomas Muster to seven successive wins when he knocked the top-seeded Austrian out of the $635,000 Qatar Open on Friday.

Courier's 6-3 7-5 quarter-final victory extended a sequence stretching back to the 1992 Australian Open and put the American, who has won four Grand Slam titles in his career and is seeded eighth here, into the semifinals against twice French Open winner Sergi Bruguera of Spain.
Courier thrived in windy conditions while Muster said he had not fully recovered from a marathon second round win over Christian Ruud on Thursday night.
"I'm used to playing in a stiff breeze so it doesn't worry me," said Courier, who built up for this tournament at his Miami home.

"Even though I've beeten Thomas seven times in succession now, I still know that I have to play well to beat him. I've got three good matches under my belt here now and I'm very satisfied with the direction I'm heading in, especially so early in the season," added Courier, who has yet to drop a set in the tournament.
Muster broke Courier in the first game but the American returned the compliment and broke decisively in the eighth game.
Courier broke through again in the 11th game of the second set before wrapping up victory after 87 minutes.
"Jim has always played well against me, so it's not a big surprise that he won," said Muster.
"Today, he had fewer unforced errors and was focused on what he was doing. I have not played a lot outdoors recently and I had a lot of trouble recovering from my second round match.
"It took me a long time to get going in this match and you can't afford a slow start against a player like Jim," said Muster, who once again needed treatment on his injured ankle.

Bruguera booked his semi-final spot with a 6-1 2-6 6-3 win over defending champion and sixth seed Petr Korda of the Czech Republic while unheralded Moroccan Hicham Arazi knocked out Sweden's Magnus Larsson 7-6 7-6.
Arazi will meet Tim Henman of Britain who beat Swedish fifth seed Magnus Gustafsson 6-3 7-6.
